TASK
Predict each conjunction's final collision probability from CDMs issued ≥2 days before TCA, on the ESA Kelvins dataset (11,942 events, 323 high-risk).
PHASE 4 · SCORING OUR OWN LIVE CONJUNCTIONS (EXPERIMENTAL)
The bridge (ml/features.bridge_from_screener) is implemented: it maps a live screener event into the model's feature space and scores it. But our TLE screener can honestly produce only 9 of the model's 110 features — the rest, including the model's single most important input (the prior CDM risk estimate) and all orbit-determination-quality columns, have no TLE-derived source and are imputed. With those missing, the learned score is near-constant across events, so it is not surfaced per-conjunction (it would be misleading). It is kept in the report JSON for research. The honest conclusion: a covariance-based Pc (see the Conjunctions tab) is the right live risk signal today; the learned model needs real CDMs to add value. That gap is the point.
PIPELINE
01

Propagatepropagate.py

Every object on one shared inertial frame (SGP4). Same frame is the invariant that makes pairwise distances meaningful.

02

Screenscreen.py

A KD-tree returns exactly the pairs a brute-force O(n²) scan would — verified, then run at scale.

03

Refinerefine.py

Analytic close-approach: from relative position/velocity, ΔT = −(r·v)/|v|², miss = |r + v·ΔT|. Exact for linear relative motion.

04

Pcrisk_pc.py

Foster 2-D probability of collision: project the combined covariance onto the encounter plane (⟂ relative velocity) and integrate a 2-D Gaussian over the hard-body disk. Public TLEs carry no covariance, so we use a documented assumed RTN covariance — Pc is an order-of-magnitude estimate, and we also report the worst-case max-Pc.

05

Rankrisk.py

A geometric proxy (closing speed / miss, log-scaled 0–100) for quick triage, shown alongside Pc.

Reproduce every check: python -m orbitguard.validate · python tests/test_pipeline.py (9/9). Rigor and reproducibility are the point — see the About page for scope and honest limits.

We independently reproduce SOCRATES' soonest conjunctions (its objects, our freshly-fetched TLEs, our propagation + Pc). Miss distances agree to ~936 m median — order-of-magnitude agreement against the reference; larger scatter comes from element-set freshness (volatile debris), not method error. Max-Pc uses SOCRATES' documented RTN covariance (100/300/100 m) for an apples-to-apples comparison. This validates the physics, not just our internal math.
WHAT IT IS

An open, transparent, reproducible reference implementation of an autonomous conjunction-screening + ML-risk pipeline. It pulls a live CelesTrak snapshot (16,103 objects this run), propagates every object on one inertial frame, screens the whole catalogue for close approaches, refines each to a precise time and miss distance, and ranks by risk — every step validated and inspectable.

Technical reviewers

An end-to-end system with real validation and an ML head — judged on method, not marketing.

Researchers & students

A reproducible astrodynamics + ML baseline; the ESA Kelvins CDM work is built in.

Agency research / education

ESA ran the Kelvins challenge we train on; a legible open reference for R&D and outreach.

Scope: a screening / analysis demonstrator on public TLEs — not an operational or safety-certified system, and not a replacement for covariance-based services (CARA, SOCRATES, commercial SSA). Public TLEs are ~km-accurate and carry no covariance, so the Pc is a Foster 2-D probability under an assumed covariance — an order-of-magnitude estimate, cross-checked against SOCRATES in Methodology. Validate against CelesTrak SOCRATES before any operational use.
